title: Like and Get Paid
intro: A message offers you money for liking and reviewing videos. It starts with a small free payment.
Tap anything that looks odd to sniff it closer. Pin what is suspicious, clear what is harmless.
When you are sure, decide what to do.

notify.text: Earn per task: like and review videos

screen.context: You did not sign up for anything.

msg: and get paid £45 right now to see it works.

tasks.label: Pay for liking videos
tasks.lens: Liking videos does not create value for anyone.
tasks.why: Real jobs pay for real work. Fake task jobs pay for clicks.

per.label: A good pay per tiny task
per.why: Pay far out of proportion to the work is bait.

first.label: A small free payment first
first.lens: They pay £45 to make you trust them.
first.why: The small payment is bait. The big losses come after.

group.label: A private group for "bigger tasks"
group.lens: They move you to a group where the pressure grows.
group.why: A private group is where the deposits begin.

link.label: A sign-up link
link.lens: It goes to a page that is not a company site.
link.why: Check for a real company before joining anything.

noexp.label: No skills needed
noexp.why: A job with no requirements is not a job.

actions.label: Join the group and do the tasks
Search "like and review videos for pay" for warnings
Report the number and delete it

block_report.line: Reported and deleted. Your phone company can block the next one.

verify.line: Consumer advice describes exactly this scam: small payouts, then a demand for money. Case cracked.

ignore.line: You stayed safe. But the same scam is still landing on other people.

go_ahead.line: The first £45 arrived. Then "bigger tasks" needed a deposit, and the deposits never came back.

what_if.go_ahead: Real jobs never make you pay to keep earning. A small payout first is the hook.
what_if.ignore: Reporting takes two taps and helps protect other people.
what_if.verify: Checking was smart. Reporting it as well helps protect other people.

golden_rule: Money for liking videos, with a small payout first, is a task scam. Real jobs never make you pay to keep earning.

quick_check.q: A message pays you £45 for 3 easy tasks and invites you to a group for bigger ones. What is true?

options.text: It is a good side job
The small payout builds trust before a demand for money
It is risk-free if you stop early

quick_check.explain: Task scams pay a little to make you trust, then ask for deposits.

hints.nudge: Who gains when you like a video, and why would they pay you?

rows.v: Pay a little at first, then ask for money
Never make you pay to start earning
